classification.difficultyReason: Combines tangent and normal equations with axis intercepts, a sketch, a base length and a triangle area.

content.prompt: The tangent and normal to $f(x)=9-x^2$ at the point $K(1,8)$ meet the $x$-axis at $A$ and $B$ respectively. Sketch the situation, find the equations of the tangent and normal, find the coordinates of $A$ and $B$, and hence find the length $AB$ and the area of $\triangle AKB$.

answer.short: Tangent: $y=-2x+10$. Normal: $y=\frac{x}{2}+\frac{15}{2}$. $A(5,0)$, $B(-15,0)$; $AB=20$ units; area of $\triangle AKB=80$ square units. See sketch.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=-2x\\m_{\mathrm{tangent}}&=f'(1)=-2\\m_{\mathrm{normal}}&=-\frac{1}{-2}=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Tangent through $K(1,8)$:
$$\begin{align*}y-8&=-2(x-1)\\y&=-2x+10\end{align*}$$
Normal through $K(1,8)$:
$$\begin{align*}y-8&=\frac12(x-1)\\y&=\frac{x}{2}+\frac{15}{2}\end{align*}$$
At the $x$-intercepts, $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}0&=-2x+10\\x&=5\end{align*}$$
Thus $A=(5,0)$.
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac{x}{2}+\frac{15}{2}\\x&=-15\end{align*}$$
Thus $B=(-15,0)$.
$$\begin{align*}AB&=5-(-15)\\AB&=20\text{ units}\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular height from $K$ to the $x$-axis is $8$ units.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle AKB&=\frac12\times20\times8\\\text{Area of }\triangle AKB&=80\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
